messages:
anya: FYI noticed a burst of tiny host->GPU migrations around 03:07 UTC causing p95 latency blips. looks like fragmentation + instantaneous watermark reaction.
devon: do we know if it was triggered by eviction or proactive migration?
anya: migration controller. pool host_free_mb dipped briefly -> full scan -> many small moves. concurrent migrations spiked.
sam: numbers?
anya: host_migration_rate=95/min, avg_migration_size=2.8MB, concurrent_peak=14, median_pause=18ms. infra-bot: alert: host_pool_pressure (pool=staging-us-central, duration=70s)
natalie: small average size + high rate => allocator fragmentation + threshold hysteresis problem.
devon: proposal: add a damping window and rate-limits to migration controller. specifics:
- EWMA on host pressure (configurable alpha)
- rate-limit concurrent migrations per-tenant
- coalesce candidate tensors owned by same tenant when contiguous in allocator buckets
- add migration lease to avoid refcount races when delaying moves
sam: coalescing sounds useful but risky. controller-level coalesce first, not allocator rewrite. track peak memory increase metric.
anya: draft config:
```
migration:
  ewma_alpha: 0.15
  min_backoff_ms: 40
  max_backoff_ms: 400
  max_concurrent_per_tenant: 3
  coalesce_bucket_bytes: 65536
  migration_lease_ms: 250
```
devon: +observability: add coalesced_migration_size histogram, migration_reason label, sampled_allocator_snapshot 1/2000.
natalie: rollout: feature-flag + canary in staging-us-central, 48h A/B. watch migration_rate, host_stall_ms, tenant_p95, OOM_rate.
sam: open questions: per-tenant EWMA vs global; safe defaults for max_concurrent; exact coalesce heuristics (same-owner + same-bucket + size cap).
anya: my preference: per-tenant EWMA with global fallback, controller coalesce first, conservative defaults. I'll file RFC and include incident trace.
infra-bot: task created: rfc/migration-damping (owner=anya), telemetry/migration-coalesce (owner=devon), canary/flag (owner=sam)
anya: thanks all, will post RFC link when ready. :thumbsup:
